Nearest PRE counterpart is TikTok. Tested all four transformation tiers: Narrowed (Amazon storefront is a specific way of being TikTok — FALSE, different platform types); Reframed (do they share a semantic territory with a shifted frame? — NO, content distribution vs commerce sales are different functional domains, not sibling frames on the same territory); Elaborated (POST does not keep TikTok intact and add detail — POST introduces a separately chosen commerce platform); Expanded (does POST broaden TikTok into a broader multi-platform seed? — NO, Amazon storefront is a distinct platform with its own functional role, not a broadened version of TikTok). TikTok remains a content platform; Amazon storefront is a separately added commerce channel. Different conceptual domains. Removed + New is the correct outcome. Per Stage 3, this pairing (if attempted) would be correctly rejected. Confirm.

semantic_events.rationale: The Amazon storefront is a commerce-based platform with no antecedent in the PRE. Nearest PRE counterpart (TikTok) was tested against all four transformation tiers and failed: different platform types (content vs commerce), no shared semantic territory at a non-umbrella level, not a detail added to TikTok, and not a broadened version of TikTok (Amazon storefront is a distinct, separately chosen commerce platform). TikTok remains in a matched pair, so restore_lineage is structurally unavailable. Different conceptual domains warrant Removed + New.
semantic_events.alternative_considered: Expanded (TikTok broadened into a multi-platform commerce-adjacent strategy) — rejected because Amazon storefront is a separately chosen commerce platform, not a broadened version of TikTok; the two retain distinct functional roles.
